title: Public art funding for Langs Drive redevelopment
subtitle: Moody's credit rating update, development charge adequacy report, and a short agenda with no delegations.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that up to $150,000 from the Public Art Reserve go to a permanent public artwork at the Langs Drive Redevelopment in Cambridge {{vote:m1}}. Staff said the money comes from a reserve set aside for this purpose and has no impact on the tax levy. Council still needs to adopt the recommendation.

The committee also received several reports for information. These included the Moody's credit rating update, the Development Charge Adequacy Report and the Council/Committee tracking list. On the credit rating, staff said they will look into the Region's debt levels compared with other municipalities and report back. A report on long-term fiscal sustainability is expected next month.

For residents, the main point is how the Region uses dedicated reserves for public art in a new housing development while budget pressures remain a concern. The committee's next meeting is October 8, 2024.

decisions.item: Public art for Langs Drive Redevelopment
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve up to $150,000 from the Public Art Reserve for a permanent public artwork at 589 Langs Drive, Cambridge {{vote:m1}}.

debate: One councillor said some residents see $150,000 for public art as a poor signal when households are struggling with grocery bills and a possible 13% regional tax increase. The councillor still supported Langs and public art in general but felt the timing was difficult.
Other councillors answered that the money comes from a reserve dedicated to public art and has zero impact on the tax levy, so it is unrelated to the budget challenges.

Supporters said the site suits public art: it is a busy street, across from a school, and will house a youth centre. Some said the project shows equity, since all developments, including Waterloo Region housing, deserve art.

On the Moody's update, a councillor asked whether the Region is close to carrying too much debt. Staff said Moody's had flagged debt levels to monitor but kept the AAA rating. Another councillor noted that the Region ranks weakest on the debt-to-reserve ratio among the municipalities charted, and that a lower reserve balance could worsen it.

A councillor questioned Moody's description of high provincial and federal operating funding, given the Region's view that it covers costs that should be funded by other levels of government. Staff said it refers to pandemic-era transfers and the likelihood of senior government support in an emergency.
